items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: He played in Woody Herman’s first Herd and with a long list of great jazz soloists, including Lee Konitz, Lennie Tristano, Benny Goodman and J.J. Johnson.

ctx.x: Guitarist Billy Bauer defines the word versatility. His career has included work with big bands, small swing combos and experimental jazz ensembles. He was born in New York on November 14, 1915 and learned the banjo at an early age.

Billy was able to use his music to work during the depression years and became a full time musician by his early twenties. He played in Woody Herman’s first Herd and with a long list of great jazz soloists, including Lee Konitz, Lennie Tristano, Benny Goodman and J.J. Johnson. Billy was a member of the Metronome All Stars from 1947-53 and was on staff with the NBC Orchestra.
He has authored a book entitled Sideman, and shares his experience in the world of jazz with students at his guitar studio on Long Island.
